correctness.rationale: Static shattering cannot query two different colors at one vertex, establishing VC<=n. With two colors only two proper colorings exist, so both dimensions equal one. For q=3, any four consecutive targeted positions cannot all be shattered: all-ones makes targets proper; both 101 triple patterns force alternating target colors a,b,a,b, after which 1001 cannot be realized with proper adjacent internal colors. Disjoint four-vertex blocks force floor(n/4) unqueried vertices. Conversely query each first-three-of-four block with alternating 1,2,1 targets; each binary labeling of a run length <=3 is feasible, and the one unqueried separator can take a third color distinct from both neighboring runs. For q>=4, alternating (1,2) target and (3,4) off-target colors give any n-bit pattern. For all q>=3, adaptive prefix choices give a full n-level binary mistake tree; for any partial assignment family, each splitting positive branch fixes one previously unfixed coordinate, giving Ldim<=n by induction. Independently enumerated proper coloring hypotheses and computed VC/Ldim for q2 n<=5,q3 n<=5,q4 n<=3; direct argument handles all n.
residual_risks: Proof assumes only binary equality literal queries, not revelation of an entire vertex color.
The q=3 four-position obstruction is a local feasibility argument, not a general graph theorem.

value.rationale: The palette size at which a connected graph of maximum degree two acquires a linearly growing adaptive-versus-nonadaptive shattering gap is a natural complete classification in concept learning. The q=3 four-consecutive-vertex obstruction and q>=4 alternate-color construction explain a genuine combinatorial transition, not a generic counting bound. Its precise linear gap floor(n/4) is needed to understand interaction between coloring constraints and one-hot query semantics.
residual_risks: Result depends on one-hot membership queries and might change for full-color queries or general graphs.

final_claim: For proper q-coloring one-hot literal concepts of labeled path P_n, n>=1, q>=2, Littlestone dimension is 1 if q=2 and n if q>=3, while VC dimension is 1 if q=2, n−floor(n/4) if q=3, and n if q>=4. Thus an unbounded Ldim−VCdim gap occurs exactly at q=3.
limitations: All n>=1 and integer q>=2, proper colorings of P_n only, one-hot equality literals.
No higher graph-degree or different learning-target theorem is asserted.
